classification.difficultyReason: Apply the vertical line test to supplied graphs, distinguishing repeated intersections from single outputs. The hardest decisions are interpreting the open and closed endpoints in (i) and recognising that the excluded input in (j) does not prevent the graph representing a function.

content.prompt: Determine whether the following relations are also functions.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with vertex at the axes' intersection, arrows at both curve ends, no numerical scale.
spec.mathematics: Each vertical line intersects the parabola at most once. The unscaled drawing uses a quadratic model without supplying an equation to students.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the parabola at most once, so it passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Vertical line through x=2, with arrows at both ends and labelled coordinate axes.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=2$ contains many graph points. One input has multiple outputs, so the graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Horizontal line y=1 with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Every input has the single output 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets $y=1$ exactly once, so it passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Unit circle with all four axis intercepts labelled.
spec.mathematics: x^2+y^2=1. Interior vertical lines meet the circle twice.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=0$ meets the circle at $y=1$ and $y=-1$, so the graph fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Sinusoidal graph with two complete cycles, closed endpoints at -2π and 2π, vertical labels ±1.
spec.mathematics: The supplied shape is represented by y=sin(x) on [-2π,2π], preserving both crests, both troughs and passage through the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the curve at most once, so it passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Upper unit semicircle with closed endpoints, x-axis labels -1, 0 and 1, no apex value.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Each vertical line meets the upper semicircle at most once, including the closed endpoints.

spec.description: Left unit semicircle with closed endpoints on the y-axis at ±1.
spec.mathematics: x=-sqrt(1-y^2). Vertical lines through the interior meet two points.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: A vertical line through the interior of the left semicircle meets it twice, so it fails the vertical line test.

spec.description: Decreasing S-shaped curve with horizontal tangent at the origin and arrows at both ends. No numerical scale.
spec.mathematics: An unscaled decreasing cubic model preserves the source's graphical classification.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the decreasing curve at most once, so it passes the vertical line test.

spec.description: Leftward ray y=0 with open origin and rightward ray y=1 with closed endpoint at x=0.
spec.mathematics: y=0 for x<0 and y=1 for x≥0. The open origin excludes a second output at x=0.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph and endpoint states visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Each vertical line meets one included point. At $x=0$, the open circle excludes $y=0$ and the filled point includes $y=1$.

spec.description: Two reciprocal-shaped branches in quadrants I and III, with four continuation arrows and no numerical scale.
spec.mathematics: A positive reciprocal model preserves the branches and asymptotes. Each x in the domain has one y.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the graph at most once. The line $x=0$ has no intersection and lies outside the domain.

spec.description: V-shaped graph with vertex at the origin and upward continuation arrows, without numerical scale.
spec.mathematics: An unscaled absolute-value model preserves the source's shape.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the V-shaped graph exactly once, including at the vertex.

spec.description: Three closed loops meeting at the origin, with two upper loops and a narrow lower loop reaching y=-1. A parametric drawing preserves the visible topology and symmetry without adding a student-visible equation.
spec.mathematics: Some vertical lines intersect more than one loop point.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible in all editions.

answer.worked: Some vertical lines intersect the loops more than once, so the graph fails the vertical line test.
